title: Here are 5 newborn sleep tips that actually help:  1.Offer feedings e...
description: Here are 5 newborn sleep tips that actually help:  1.Offer feedings every 2-3 hours during the day, according to hunger cues. Yes! Wake them if it’s been longer than 3 hours since their last feed during the day.  2.Offer a nap after about 60-90 minutes of awake time. (This includes the feeding). Which leads me to the next tip… 3.Try to make the feeding an awake time activity. Snoozing during the feeding makes naps and nights harder. I know this isn’t easy. Strip them down, change their diaper, wipe a cloth over their face, stimulate their feet, etc.  4.Take them back to the womb when you want them to sleep! Make it dark. Swaddle them so they feel snug and secure. Turn on a sound machine. (Yes, this feels familiar to them!)  5.Take a sleep class! Truly, watching all of this in action (plus so much more) with real newborns is like having a manual for your newborn. Parents of newborns swear that this class has changed their lives. title: All that movement and noise is called "active sleep." This is similar...
description: All that movement and noise is called "active sleep." This is similar to REM sleep for adults, but with one HUGE difference. During REM sleep, an adult’s skeletal muscles are PARALYZED. Babies’ muscles are not! They move, make noise, cry out, and even open their eyes! BUT, active sleep is still actually SLEEPING! 💤 ⁣ So, before you intervene, STOP and observe. 🛑 👀  Give it about 30-60 seconds. This will help you determine if your baby is just transitioning between sleep cycles or if your baby is TRULY awake!  Have you ever seen this with your little one? title: In the last months of pregnancy, a baby’s muscles begin to strengthen...
description: In the last months of pregnancy, a baby’s muscles begin to strengthen and curl into the fetal position.  When they’re born, their muscles are still flexed (which is totally normal). That’s why their arms and legs naturally bend in, and sometimes, when you lay them down, their muscles contract. That contraction causes them to scrunch or even roll slightly to the side.  Parents often wonder if their newborn is already learning to roll, but this newborn curl is not a sign of rolling. It’s one of those sweet newborn reflexes that fades as they grow, so soak it in while it lasts! newborn scrunch | newborn curl vs rolling | newborn curl reflex | when do babies roll | newborn rolling to side | baby scrunch

If we get those reps in when they’re awake and engaged, we’re less likely to see that practice disrupt sleep!  As always, if you find yourself needing more help- I’m here for you with classes and free resources at the LIB ❤️  #sleepregression #newmilestone #newskills #babysleep

title: No, we don't swaddle 12 month olds. This was just a test. Babies MUST...
description: No, we don't swaddle 12 month olds. This was just a test. Babies MUST come out of the swaddle when they show signs of rolling. (Typically around 3 to 4 months.)  This swaddle truly is breakout proof when used correctly!  Why does that matter?  Well, if babies bust out of the swaddle: the swaddle becomes loose bedding that can cover the mouth or nose, which is unsafe. little arms can flail, leading to unnecessary night wakings. A breakout-proof swaddle is such a good thing!
